title: The North Wind and the Sun
text:
The North Wind and the Sun once argued about which of them was the stronger. Neither would give way, so they agreed on a test. A traveler was walking along the road below, wrapped in a cloak. Whoever could make him take it off would be the winner.

The North Wind went first. He blew a cold blast that tugged at the cloak and whipped it around the man's legs. The traveler only pulled it tighter. The Wind blew harder and harder, howling and hurling gusts until the trees bent, but the harder he blew, the more firmly the man held his cloak closed and hunched against the cold. At last the Wind gave up.

Then the Sun came out from behind a cloud and simply shone. The air grew mild, and the traveler loosened his grip. The Sun shone a little warmer, and the man opened the cloak. Soon the heat was so pleasant and then so strong that he took the cloak off entirely, and finally, overcome by the heat, he stripped further and went to bathe in a nearby stream.

The Sun had won without any struggle at all.
lesson: Pressure makes people dig in. When you want someone to change, warmth, patience and good reasons usually work far better than force.
